the author's own proof environment immediately following the lemma: The result also follows from the morphisms get-affine lemma, but a direct proof is given. Put A' = Gamma(V, O_V); then j' : V to Spec(A') is a quasi-compact open immersion by the quasi-affine lemma, and for the image f' of f the preimage (j')^{-1}D(f') = j^{-1}D(f) is affine, while j'(V) intersect V(f') is a subscheme of Spec(A') mapping isomorphically to the closed subscheme j(V) intersect V(f) of Spec(A), hence closed in Spec(A') by the section-immersion lemma. Replacing A by A' one may assume j is an open immersion with A = Gamma(V, O_V). In this case j(V) = Spec(A): otherwise a principal affine open D(g) meets the complement of j(V) and avoids the closed subset j(V) intersect V(f); since j maps j^{-1}D(f) isomorphically onto D(f) (invert-f-affine lemma), D(g) meets V(f); and j^{-1}D(g), a principal open of the affine open j^{-1}D(f), is affine, so the invert-f-affine lemma again identifies D(g) with j^{-1}D(g) inside j^{-1}D(f), forcing D(g) inside D(f), a contradiction.
